correctness.rationale: The proof reduces the Euler characteristic to a completely described projective fixed locus. A generic integral cocharacter has weight zero on the Cartan and pairwise distinct nonzero weights on root spaces. Nilpotency excludes the Cartan projective space. Weyl conjugacy and torus scaling make all root vectors of a fixed length one orbit. The standard minimal-orbit theorem places every long-root line in every nonzero nilpotent orbit closure, while the short-root lines are present exactly when the short-root-vector orbit is contained. Euler localization then yields the stated count. The bundled checker verifies root counts and weight separation on all classical types through rank 12 and explicitly on F4 and G2.

value.rationale: Nilpotent orbit closures are central singular varieties in algebraic geometry and geometric representation theory. The theorem collapses the ordinary Euler characteristic of every nonzero projectivized orbit closure in a fixed simple Lie algebra to one value in simply laced types and at most two values in all other types. The dichotomy has a structural explanation entirely in terms of root lengths and the minimal orbit, and it applies uniformly across arbitrarily many orbit closures. This is a natural global invariant of the projective singularities themselves, complementary to the extensive literature on symplectic, crepant, and contact resolutions.
